skill.name: changelog-generator
skill.description: Generate release changelogs from git commit history using Conventional Commits, Keep a Changelog sections, and semantic version guidance.
skill.summary: Turns git commits into structured release notes and version recommendations.
skill.author: CuriousLearner

security_audit.summary: The skill is mostly release documentation guidance, but it includes executable Bash, Node.js, Python, and GitHub Actions examples. The main risks are shell command construction with unquoted git references and scripts that write CHANGELOG.md. I found no prompt injection attempt or malicious exfiltration intent.

remediation.issue: Unquoted git reference interpolation in shell commands
remediation.suggestion: Pass git arguments as arrays, validate tag names, and quote shell expansions before execution.
Require explicit user confirmation and provide a dry-run or backup before overwriting files.

remediation.issue: Unescaped commit text in generated release notes
remediation.suggestion: Escape Markdown metacharacters and review generated links before publishing release notes.

semantic_findings.title: Unescaped Commit Text in Release Notes
semantic_findings.description: The examples copy commit subjects and bodies into changelog entries and release bodies without escaping Markdown. A crafted commit message could create misleading links, mentions, or rendered content in published release notes.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Commit messages are parsed as text and appended directly to Markdown or GitHub release output. Impact depends on the renderer, so confidence is high for the behavior but moderate for exploitability.

content.value_statement: Release notes take time and can miss important commit details. This skill groups git commits into clear changelog sections with version guidance.
actual_capabilities: Classifies Conventional Commit types into changelog sections.
Highlights breaking changes and deprecations before other changes.
Suggests major, minor, or patch version changes.
Produces Keep a Changelog style Markdown entries.
Shows Bash, Node.js, Python, and GitHub Actions automation examples.
Supports hash, author, version, and since-tag options in examples.
limitations: Works best when commit messages follow Conventional Commits.
Generated entries still need human release review.
Example scripts may modify CHANGELOG.md if copied and run.
Shell examples need hardening before use with untrusted repositories.

use_cases.title: Prepare Release Notes
use_cases.description: Create a release-ready changelog from recent git commits and group changes by user impact.

use_cases.title: Automate Changelog Updates
use_cases.description: Add repeatable changelog generation to package scripts or CI release workflows.

use_cases.title: Assess Version Impact
use_cases.description: Review commit history for breaking changes and choose a semantic version bump.

prompt_templates.title: Create Basic Changelog
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate a Keep a Changelog entry from commits since the latest tag. Group changes by type and flag breaking changes.

prompt_templates.title: Add Release Metadata
prompt_templates.prompt: Create release notes for version 1.4.0. Include commit hashes, authors, dates, and separate sections for fixes and features.

prompt_templates.title: Recommend Version Bump
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze commits since v1.3.2 and recommend the next semantic version. Explain any breaking changes and migration notes.

prompt_templates.title: Design Safe Automation
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a secure changelog automation workflow. Include dry-run review, safe git argument handling, and explicit approval before file writes.

output_examples.input: Commits include feature export support, timezone fixes, and setup documentation updates.
output_examples.output: Added: export support. Fixed: timezone parsing. Documentation: setup guide updates. Suggested version: minor.

output_examples.input: A release contains a breaking authentication change and a token refresh fix.
output_examples.output: Breaking changes appear first with migration notes. The suggested version is a major release.

output_examples.input: A maintainer asks for unreleased changes since v2.1.0 with authors included.
output: The release owner receives a review-ready draft.

best_practices: Review generated entries for customer impact before release.
Use Conventional Commits consistently with clear scopes.
Run automation on a test branch before writing CHANGELOG.md.
anti_patterns: Do not publish raw commit subjects without editing unclear wording.
Do not run shell snippets against untrusted tags without quoting.
Do not treat version suggestions as final without release owner review.

faq.question: Does this require Conventional Commits?
faq.answer: It works best with Conventional Commits, but it can group other commit messages under general change sections.

faq.question: Can it update an existing changelog?
faq.answer: The examples show how to insert new entries into CHANGELOG.md, but changes should be reviewed before saving.

faq.question: Does it choose the next version?
faq.answer: It suggests a semantic version bump based on features, fixes, and breaking changes.

faq.question: Can it run in CI?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes GitHub Actions examples for release notes and package publishing workflows.

faq.question: Does it fetch data from the internet?
faq.answer: The skill itself is guidance. Some examples reference GitHub, npm, or release actions when used in CI.

faq.question: Is the generated output ready to publish?
faq.answer: No. A maintainer should review wording, links, breaking changes, and version decisions before release.
